RewardsCompetitionsNewslettersWeather ForecastEuropeTrump says he asked Putin to ‘pull back’ military aggression throughout EuropeUS president cites possibility of peace breakthrough as White House pursues direct engagement with MoscowUS president Donald Trump speaking to reporters at the White House in Washington earlier this week.  Photograph: EPA Thu Nov 26 2026 - 17:26 • 2 MIN READUS president ‌Donald Trump said on Thursday he told Russian leader Vladimir Putin last week he would like to see Russia pull ‌back on military aggression against territories throughout Europe in the hope it could lead to a quick settlement of the ​war in Ukraine.

“During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories ​throughout Europe, in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly,” Trump wrote ⁠in a Truth Social post.

“I really believe this is a strong possibility – Thousands of ‌people ‌are ​being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH,” Trump said.

Trump has frequently urged a negotiated end to the war in Ukraine, but the ⁠phrase “territories throughout Europe” suggests territories beyond ​the battlefield in Ukraine.

Trump did not elaborate on ​what conduct he was asking Putin to halt. Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine started ‌in 2022, other countries have occasionally accused Russia ​of provocative behaviour.

Poland, a Nato member, this week accused Russia of deliberately violating Polish airspace. ⁠Estonia recently linked an arson attack to ⁠Russia’s military intelligence service.

Trump ​met Putin last week in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of the Apec leaders’ meeting, part of a diplomatic push by his administration to address the war in Ukraine and broader security issues. He also participated in a trilateral summit with Putin and Chinese president Xi Jinping.

The Trump administration has argued that direct engagement with both leaders could help reduce global tensions, while critics have questioned whether Washington is ‌applying sufficient pressure on Moscow ⁠to end the conflict.

Trump’s son-in-law and diplomatic envoy Jared Kushner on Wednesday praised Putin as a “grandmaster of politics” and a “historic figure” in a podcast interview with ‌Mathias Dopfner, chief executive of German media group Axel Springer.

Kushner argued that Putin had shown “restraint” by refraining from using nuclear ​weapons despite the risk of the Ukraine war escalating dramatically, and ​that he believed Putin wanted peace and improved relations with the United States. – Reuters
